A 21-year-old breastfeeding woman visits her primary care physician due to severe unilateral breast
pain that has progressively worsened, making it difficult for her to breastfeed from her left breast. Her
medical history includes gestational diabetes managed with diet and exercise. Vital signs reveal a
temperature of 101°F (38.3°C), blood pressure of 153/77 mmHg, pulse of 91/min, respirations of
17/min, and oxygen saturation of 97% on room air. Physical examination shows an erythematous left
breast with a 3-cm tender and fluctuant mass. What is the most appropriate next step in managing this
patient? Answer Choices: (A) Warm compresses and observation (B) Ice packs and breast pumping
(C) Oral antibiotics and continued breastfeeding (D) Core needle biopsy to confirm abscess (E) Incision
and drainage (F) Surgical excision of the mass (G) Needle biopsy to rule out inflammatory breast
cancer (H) Ultrasound and fine needle aspiration (I) Vancomycin and discharge home (J)
Mammography to evaluate for malignancy
 A. Mammography to evaluate for malignancy
B. Surgical excision of the mass
C. Core needle biopsy to confirm abscess
D. Needle biopsy to rule out inflammatory breast cancer
E. Oral antibiotics and continued breastfeeding
F. Ultrasound and fine needle aspiration
G. Ice packs and breast pumping
H. Warm compresses and observation
I. Incision and drainage
J. Vancomycin and discharge home
